episode_title: Episode #35: Don’t Buy Another CNC Machine Until You Run Lights Out

real_qa.q: How can machine shops increase profitability by running lights out manufacturing without requiring a second shift?
real_qa.r: By standardizing tooling, tool holding, work holding, and programming to create a stable repeatable process, shops can run parts unattended overnight. Even just one hour per day unattended equals about 250 hours per year, which at $100 per hour shop rate generates $25,000 in additional revenue. The key is that unattended machining generates unburdened money because your shop rate changes for those off-hours—the spindle and compressor run at minimal cost versus the full burden applied during an eight-hour day.
real_qa.requete: lights out manufacturing profitability machine shop

real_qa.q: What is the real cause of the talent gap in machine shops and tool and die manufacturing according to industry operators?
real_qa.r: The real gap is not necessarily in young people entering the field, but in experienced trainers available to teach them. When a 10-year period saw declining interest in machining, the experienced operators who had spent that decade running shops were not available to train newcomers. Private equity firms buying shops have accelerated this by firing long-tenured employees—one PE firm fired a worker with 43 years of experience—and replacing them with MBAs unfamiliar with shop operations, making it impossible to train entry-level workers without existing experience.
real_qa.requete: machine shop talent gap training experienced operators

real_qa.q: How can small shops with limited part volume still benefit from unattended lights out machining?
real_qa.r: Volume is not a prerequisite—cycle time is what matters. A shop can run even a single complex part unattended if the cycle is long enough. One example was a single weldment plate with 54 quarter-20 tapped holes thread-milled overnight, taking an hour and a half to two hours unattended. By stacking three thread mills and assigning 17-18 holes per tool without relying on tool life management, the machine ran completely unattended, freeing the operator and eliminating the need for human presence.
real_qa.requete: lights out machining low volume parts single job

real_qa.q: What is the financial impact of increasing part density with fixtures for lights out production runs?
real_qa.r: Creating fixtures that hold multiple parts (e.g., two fixtures holding 20 parts each for 40 total parts per cycle) dramatically improves hourly rate and margin. With $10 labor per part, 40 parts running five minutes each yields 3.3 hours of cycle time at $121 per hour ($400 revenue). At night unattended, the only cost is spindle and compressor (~$10/hour), so margin grows significantly. Running such a job for a week generates $2,000 in unattended revenue, potentially paying for the fixture entirely.
real_qa.requete: fixture part density lights out machining margin calculation

real_qa.q: What specific tool life data and machine monitoring capabilities are required to safely run lights out machining overnight?
real_qa.r: You must have reliable data on tool life and know exactly how long tools can run before degrading. For example, high feed cutters in 4340 steel can run 2.5 to 3 hours before becoming unpredictable; pushing to four hours risks tool detonation. Tool breakage detection is essential—without it, a broken tool will destroy subsequent tools as they contact the same cavity. Modern machines can send SMS alerts when tool breakage occurs, but you must also manually verify coolant levels, oil levels, and anti-foam additives before running overnight to avoid flooding the tank or running dry.
real_qa.requete: tool breakage detection lights out machining overnight safety
